Evidence of female literacy in this language is contained in such corpora as the Wooing Group and the Katherine Group. The merging of dialects in this language caused the loss of distinction between the present participle and the gerund, while the lengthening of first-syllable vowels in words composed of two short syllables led to the muting of final "e." This language's writing system included an all-purpose character for velar sounds, which resembles a cursive "z" and is called "yogh." This language existed for most of its lifespan alongside French and Latin, and became the sole tongue during the transition to its successor, the "Early Modern" phase. Perhaps the most well-known text in this language begins "Whan that Aprill, with his shoures soote." identify this language, which flourished from around 1070 to 1500 in the British Isles.

This man wrote that "sunlight is said to be the best of disinfectants" in a book which publicized the findings of the Pujo committee. He exposed the ways bankers used borrowed money to further their own interests. This author of Other People's Money fought against the merger of the New Haven and Boston and Maine railroads. With Samuel Warren, he wrote the influential article "The Right to Privacy," a theme he would press in arguing for "the right to be left alone" in an opinion for a case that ruled wiretapping unconstitutional. Before opposing the Olmstead case, he wrote a document which used sociological and medical data to argue in favor of work limits in Muller v. Oregon. Name this Jewish Supreme Court Justice who authored a namesake "brief."

This man lost power after attempting to annex the region of Kagera, but escaped death with the help of Libya's Muammar al-Gaddafi. He gained power by executing a coup while his predecessor was in a Singapore meeting of the Commonwealth of Nations. This man expelled all the Asians in the country he ruled, crippling the economy. He both succeeded and was basically succeeded by Milton Obote. He lost power after invading Tanzania led by Julius Nyerere. Along with saying that Hitler was "right to burn six million Jews," this man allowed a Palestinian liberation group to hijack an Air France airplane. Israel responded with Operation Thunderbolt, which saw most hostages return safely from Entebbe Airport. Name this dictator of Uganda who may have been a cannibal.

In one action, this man won a battle to prevent his opponent from taking Pskov. According to the Livonian Rhymed Chronicle, this man had a 60 to one advantage in men in that battle. This man served as an intermediary between the various Russian rulers and the Mongols under Sartaq Khan of the Golden Horde, whose support made it possible for this man to become Grand Prince of Vladimir. However, this leader of the Republic of Novgorod gained his epithet after defeating the Swedes at the Battle of the Neva River in 1240 and for his defeat of the Knights of the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Lake Peipus or the Battle of the Ice two years later. Identify this Russian ruler who is the subject and namesake of a famous 1938 Sergei Eisenstein film.

Jaroslav Dabrowski led this polity's military. It established a one hundred percent inheritance tax and a ban on prostitution and night work in bakeries. One incident during this polity saw General Lecomte attempt to commandeer some artillery pieces, only for his soldiers to disobey and for the Mayor of Montmarte to be powerless to stop Generals Thomas and Lecomte's deaths. The flag of Vietnam was inspired by this polity's monochrome red banner. Marshal MacMahon helped to end it. Much of its territory was set on fire during the "Bloody Week." Although Louis Auguste Blanqi was elected its leader, Adolphe Thiers captured him, making Blanqui unable to lead it. Identify this body that controlled the French capital in the aftermath of the Franco-Prussian War.

This man built an alliance with fellow countryman Daniele Mann at the Congress of Paris. Before getting banished from the court, he spent his early years as the page of Charles Albert, and his first name derives from his godfather, the husband of Pauline Bonaparte. This man negotiated a deal reached at Plombieres where his country gave up Nice in exchange for French military support. His political alliance with Urbano Ratazzi allowed him to oust rival Massimo D'Azeglio from power. Responsible for persuading the Piedmontese parliament to proclaim that Victor Emanuel II was King of Italy, he had earlier founded the newspaper, Il Risogimento. Name this active figure in Italian unification.

One historian addressed the problem of censorship regarding this event in No Breathing Room, a work that was introduced by David Marples, who wrote of its "Social Impact". The causes of this event were detailed in the INSAG-1 Report. It was not publicly disclosed until evidence of it was found in a facility in Forsmark, and the name of the Worm Wood Forest was changed after this event. It partially occurred because the ECCS and Local Automatic Control Systems were turned off, and it prompted the creation of the Zone of Alienation. It was exacerbated by an experiment carried out in Unit 4, and could not be prevented by a brief release of steam from the relief valves. Resulting in the abandonment of the town of Pryp'yat in 1986, name this meltdown of at a Soviet nuclear power plant.

This group often held councils around a sacred stew pot, and its members held kitchen-themed titles like the First Maker of Soup. This group rejected the creation of the "New Order" which would have reformed them. One revolt by this group was partially due to their feeling that the Chief Black Eunuch was trying to replace them, as well as a gripe that they hadn't been properly paid for their actions in Khotyn in 1621. After new recruits joined this group, a tail was added to their white felt cap. In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan. This group was dissolved and replaced with a more modernized corps. During the Auspicious Incident orchestrated by Mahmud II. Name this group of Ottoman soldiers originally made up of captured Christian youths.

This country gained the Protectorate of Wituland in the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty. A perceived treaty violation by king Ovonramwen and the cessation of palm oil trading led forces from this country to destroy the Kingdom of Benin. One of its colonies was depicted on the Zuniga Map and is the subject of a theory known as the "Lumbee Connection." This country's colony at Surat was founded after it won the battle of Swally, but was only profitable until this country acquired Bombay as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry. This country administered its colonies of Malacca, Penang, and Labuan under the Straights Settlement, which also encompassed Singapore. Name this country which won Gibraltar from Spain at Utrecht and established colonies at Roanoke and Jamestown.

One kingdom in the southern portion of this modern day nation had a capital at Indrapura and was ruled by King Indravarman II. Later, that kingdom's capital moved to Vijaya. In addition to the Champa kingdom, a kingdom in the northern portion of this nation fought off the Mongols at the Hong River. The unification of this nation came with the Tay S?n brothers who defeated the northern Trinhs, and again with the rise of Emperor Gia Long. Earlier, this nation gained freedom from Chinese domination with the battle of B?ch ?ang River. This nation fought off the Yongle Emperor under Le L?i and the Han dynasty under the Tr?ng Sisters. Name this nation reunified again after the capture of Saigon with capital at Hanoi.

He dispatched several warships to Morocco after the bandit Raisuli kidnapped the Greek-American Ion Perdicaris. This politician railed against the "doctrine of ignoble ease" in a speech titled "The Strenuous Life." As president, his foreign policy initiatives included sending out the Great White Fleet and dispatching naval forces to support an independence movement against Colombia. He signed the Elkins and Hepburn Acts, which enforced the limitation of large companies as an aspect of his Square Deal. This man became the only third party candidate to place second in a presidential election when he ran on the Bull Moose ticket in 1912. Name this American president who fought with the Rough Riders during the Spanish American War and who popularized the phrase "Speak softly and carry a big stick."

This man encouraged collective farms to expel their useless members while serving as Party Chief in Ukraine. This man was mentored by Lazar Kaganovich, who with this man supervised construction of the Moscow Metro, and led to this man becoming Party Leader for Moscow. Later, Kaganovich along with Malenkov and Molotov opposed this man as part of the Anti-Party group. More famously, this man debated in a kitchen with Richard Nixon and demanded a peace treaty between the Germanies, but failed in that endeavor, leading to the construction of the Berlin Wall. This man is best known for dealing with Kennedy in the Cuban Missile Crisis and for being succeeded by Brezhnev. Name this man who in the "Secret Speech" condemned his predecessor Stalin.

This polity was founded by the illegitimate Ramiro after the death of his father, Sancho the Great. One ruler of this polity conquered the Balearic Islands and accepted French suzerainty in the Treaty of Corbeil. In addition to James I, his son and successor Peter the Great fought against Pope Martin IV as part of the War of the Sicilian Vespers in a namesake crusade. More famously, this polity was ruled by a person who became heir to Andreas Paleologos, defeated Juana la Beltraneja, and forced Muslim subjects to convert to Christianity. One of that ruler's daughters married Philip the Handsome while another married Henry VIII. Name this polity ruled by Ferdinand II.

This man introduced a bill attempting to use the extra proceeds from the Second Bank of the United States to construct a national highway, which was vetoed by Madison and called the Bonus Bill. He created the Bureau of Indian affairs without congressional approval as Secretary of War during the Era of Good Feelings. His wife Floride provoked the Petticoat affair by ostracizing Peggy Eaton. This man was elected vice-president in 1824 despite attacking the Corrupt Bargain, and he would be elected vice-president again four years later as part of Andrew Jackson's ticket. He opposed the Tariff of Abominations by writing the South Carolina Exposition and Protest, which positioned him as a leading advocate of nullification. Name this influential South Carolina politician.

This dynasty won the Battle of Baekgang, but was earlier stymied by Yeon Gaesomun. Near the end of this dynasty, Huang Chao formed the Qi dynasty, while earlier during this dynasty, Luoyang was the capital of the Yan dynasty. Its Emperor Xianzong attempted to regain power from the jiedushior regional military governors. It allied with the Silla to end Korea's Three Kingdom's Period. It was followed by the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms, and came to power shortly after the Northern and Southern Dynasties. Emperor Xuanzong, like all of its other rulers, was a member of the Li family, and he loved Consort Yang Guifei, which led to the disastrous An Shi Rebellion. It succeeded the Sui Dynasty and was notably interrupted by China's only female ruler. Name this dynasty that saw the peak of Chinese power and lasted from 618 to 907.

A French ruler of this name and number faced the schemes of Charles the Bad along with a revolt by Etienne Marcel. However, he prudently chose Bertrand de Guesclin as his commander and his forces restored Henry of Trastamara's throne. His father was John the Good and he ruled after the Battle of Poitiers. In addition to the French Valois king nicknamed the "Wise," a Holy Roman Emperor of this name and number defeated Henry II and Francis I numerous times and fought against the Revolt of the Comuneros. He also fought against the Philip of Hesse in the Schmalkadic League along with calling the council of Trent. Name this regnal name and number whose most famous bearer was the son of Juana the Mad and saw the apex of Hapsburg influence.

This leader sponsored a trip by Gilberto Freyre that led to the publication of Adventures and Routine. This man ordered the construction of Cristo Rei, and he served alongside Presidents Antonio Carmona and Americo Thomaz. His secret police force was named the PIDE, and he fought against Nehru in Operation Vijay for control of Goa. This man also fought wars in Angola and Mozambique, and his unpopular foreign policies would lead to his successor, Marcelo Caetano, being overthrown in the Carnation Revolution. Name this Prime Minister from 1932 to 1968 who presided over the Estado Novo in Portugal.

This document claims that history proves mankind is "more disposed to suffer… than to right [itself] by abolishing the forms to which [it is] accustomed." After quoting Blackstone that "man shall pursue his own true and substantial happiness," this document goes on to list twelve points, among which are that "the equality of human rights results necessarily from the fact of the identity of the race in capabilities and responsibilities" and that a "perverted application of the Scriptures" has caused a certain group of people to be confined to "corrupt customs." Its ninth point dealt with the issue of voting, and its one hundred signers included Frederick Douglass and Elizabeth Cady Stanton. Name this 1848 document, the product of the Seneca Falls Convention.

One commander at this battle said that all his battalions charged at least four times during the battle. The prelude to this battle consisted of crafty maneuvering down the Rhine by the British, away from the Dutch and toward the forces of Marshal Tallard and the Elector of Bavaria. The major mistake of the losing side was the excessive requisitioning of troops into the namesake city. Eugene of Savoy commanded one wing of the Allies and John Churchill commanded the wing. Name this battle, that saved Vienna from being taken by the Franco-Bavarian army, the turning point of the War of Spanish Succession.

This politician said that the Soviets "put guns before butter, while we put just about everything before guns" in the "Britain Awake" speech, which was given after rising to power during the Winter of Discontent. The term "dries" refers to supporters of the economic policies of this leader, who fell after attempting to institute a "Community Charge" tax to fund local government. The IRA attempted to assassinate this prime minister in the Brighton hotel bombings. During this PM's term, Augusto Pinochet's early radar warnings helped British forces defeat General Galtieri's invasion of an island group near Tierra del Fuego. Name this Prime Minister who fought the Falklands War and was nicknamed the "Iron Lady"

This ruler allowed the Muscovy company to trade in Archangel and commissioned Saint Basil's Cathedral in Moscow to celebrate his destruction of the Kazan Khanate. This ruler was close to his deaf and mute brother Iuri and his grandmother was Sophia Paleologue. The unruly Shuisky brothers dominated the early part of this son of Vasily III's reign. After creating the streltsy, he made a state within a state that was operated by oprichiniks, as well as setting up the zemsky sobor. He caused a miscarriage in his favorite son's wife and then managed to accidently kill his son. Name this ruler of Russia that was succeeded by Boris Gudonov.

This man received a namesake tribute of 37,000 pounds after he was charged of having a connection with the killings of Lord Henry Cavendish and Thomas Henry Burke. He was the target of a forgery campaign by Richard Pigott, even though he was mostly acquitted in the House of Commons after a trial. As the leader of a Land League, he was thrown into the Kilmainham Jail for opposing a Coercion Act. His demise came after the Nonconformist movement of his political party, after seeing a letter written to John Rowley, voted him out of a position of leadership after he was married to Kitty O'Shea. A co-founder of the Irish Nationalist League, he is remembered for working with Gladstone to execute home rule for Ireland. Name this late-19th Century politician.

The majority opinion in this case notes that California's continual invocation of worthless remedies is "buttressed by the experience of other States." The dissent alludes to "untoward practical ramifications" that would be had regarding the in forma pauperis cases that relied on the legal procedure invalidated by this case. The dissent also mentions that an inability to recognize the weight carried by stare decisis made it seem like the Court "reached out" to overturn Wolf v. Colorado. This case saw Justice Clark note that "Nothing can destroy a government more quickly than its failure to observe its own laws." The Boyd and Weeks decisions provided precedents for this case, which exemplified the "fruit of the poisonous tree" doctrine with regards to a trunk of pornographic materials. Identify this case which ruled that the exclusionary rule made evidence taken by the Cleveland police inadmissible in court.

Five years before this conflict, Aniceto Vergara Albano signed a treaty allowing the other side to collect all the tax revenue between the 23rd and 24th parallels at a rate fixed for 25 years. This conflict began with the Battle of Topater and at the appropriately named Battle of the Halt of the Alliance. Prior to the beginning of this war, Antofagasta had already been occupied. However, this war was decided in naval battles such as Punta Greusa, which saw the loss of the Independencia, and the Battle of Iquique, which was the first of many raids from Miguel Grau. Grau's fortune ended at the Battle of Angamos, where his ship, the Huascar, was captured. Ended via the Treaty of Ancon, this war was fought over nitrite resources in the Atacama Desert and saw Bolivia allied with Peru. Name this war where Chile emerged victorious, named after a body of water.

Rumors that Emperor Constans II would move the capital from Constantinople to this island led to his death. Although not Egypt, its Aghlabid Dynasty was replaced by the Fatimids. A civil war in this place ended via the Treaty of Caltabellota, while Muslim rule of this place ended with the invasion of a man who would fight Alexius Comnenus at Dyrrhachium and had Bohemund as his son. In addition to Robert Guiscard, in 1282, this place experienced its namesake Vespers. Featuring cities such as Messina and its capital Palermo along with Syracuse, name this island south of Italy.

One early leader of this polity failed in his attempt to modernize the hi-tech industry via the Economic System of Socialism while also failing with the New Economic System. That leader's rule also saw the creation of Intershops and the Karl-Marx Alley. Its penultimate leader created vertically integrated production systems called combines along with heavily sponsoring sports to boost prestige. Bertolt Brecht spent his final years in this polity and Egon Krenz was its last leader. Its end came via Die Wende or The Change. The secret police in this country were the Stasi and its leaders have included Eric Honecker and Walter Ulbricht. Name this polity centered at Berlin, unlike its counterpart centered at Bonn.

This polity and Uruguay won the Battle of Caseros in the Platine War. Ernesto Geisel was a later ruler of this polity, which had a Constitution enacted in 1934. One ruler was known as the "father of the poor" for his labor legislation, while the death of Prince Imperial Afonso weakened the desire of another ruler to rule. Getuilo Vargas was a later ruler of this country, which later saw the Positivists gain power after Isabel proclaimed the unpopular abolition of slavery in the Golden Law. This polity gained independence following Napoleon's invasion of Portugal, and its royal house was of the House of Braganza. Name this polity once ruled by Pedro II with cities like Sao Paulo.

One act signed by this president was named after a man who was tortured and murdered in Wyoming and another after a man who was decapitated in Texas and provided fifteen million dollars to local authorities over a three year time span to fight a certain type of criminal offense. Another act signed by this president amended the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to alter the definition of a 180 day time-stamp that had caused a woman suing Goodyear company to have her case struck down in the Supreme Court. The Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act and the Lily Ledbetter Fair Pay Act were both passed under the tenure of this president, who reversed his predecessor's policy of cutting funding to foreign organizations that allowed abortion. Name this person who was succeeded as a Senator by Roland Burris.

This man organized a branch of the Vatan organization during en exile in Syria. His military exploits included marching his troops through the lines of Charles Harrington with his arms reversed. He used to heights of Chunuk Bair to win one battle, in which he prevailed despite the surprise landing at Suvla Bay. His forces are sometimes blamed for the Great Fire of Smyrna started after he fought off troops sent by Eleftherios Venizelos. He eventually grew frustrated with the "Union and Progress Party," writing the Amasya Circular which called for the Sivas Congress. He mandated the use of surnames, abolished the position of Caliph, and banned the fez as part of modernizations enacted after the fall of Mehmed VI. Name this father of modern Turkey.

This man gave a series of sermons at the Oetenbach convent which were published in the volume he Clarity and Certainty of the Word of God. His closest allies were his friend Leo Jud and eventual successor Heinrich Bullinger, who joined him in serving sausage during Lent in clear defiance of the church. He published the Sixty Seven Articles, which included his firm insistence that the act of the Eucharist is clearly symbolic, a view which would clash with Luther's doctrine of the real presence at the Marburg Colloquy. He was opposed by Johann Eck, who organized the cantons of Uri, Schwyz, and Zug against him during the Kappel Wars. Name this religious leader from Zurich and reformer of Switzerland.

This battle saw cavalry capture High Wood in the Battle of Bazentin Ridge. This battle began with the detonation of a 40,000 pound mine under the Hawthorn Ridge Redoubt in the Battle of the Albert. Although not Tannenberg, on August 29th, the Germans put Hindenburg and Ludendorff in charge, leading to the Hindenburg Line. While artillery bombardment was not very effective against German bunkers, barbed wire was easily destroyed by the newly deployed Mark I. The allies were commanded by Ferdinand Foch and Douglas Haig, and this battle also saw the first deployment of the tank. With the loss of over 350,000 British troops, name this costly 1916 World War I battle.

Aristotle approximated the time period of one ruler of this polity through evidence found on the Olympic Discus. One ruler of this polity gave Cleombrotus power in an effort to pass reforms that would redistribute land to the perioikoi. Another of its reformers introduced a council of twenty eight men over sixty years of age called the Gerousia and introduced the agoge program. Its general Pausanias led the Greek coalition forces at Plataea and was part of its Agiad family, which along with the Eurypontids provided its two kings. This city's forces were crushed by Thebans at the Battle of Leuctre. Its government included five ephors and its economy rested on the labor of helots. Name this warlike Greek city state, the major rival of Athens.

The political aspects of this war were covered in depth by David Halberstam in The Coldest Winter. A journalist for one side sparked controversy by spitting on a soldier in the Major Henderson Incident which occurred after its conclusion. Battles in the early stage of this war include one over Hill 282 and another over "the Notch." A battle at Pork Chop Hill was one of many fought over the "Iron Triangle" in this war. One side in this conflict promoted Matthew Ridgway take over command, while another side's forces were commanded by Peng Dehuai. Two opponents clashed in the Pueblo Incident fifteen years after this war ended at Panmunjeom. Name this war which saw General McArthur launch an invasion at Inchon and ended with the creation of a demilitarized zone.

This battle broke the 20 year truce of the Treaty of Vasvar and happened partly as a result of one side's support of the kuruc revolt led by Imre Thokoly. Due to the Treaty of Warsaw, the winning side received help from Polish forces, which were later augmented by the forces from a Holy League called by Innocent XI. Occurring under the reign of Leopold I, this battle saw the decisive charge of the "Winged Hussars," which finished off the host led by Kara Mustafa. Jan III Sobieski defeated the Ottomans in, what 1683 battle, which wasn't the first time the Ottomans failed to capture the capital of Austria?

This man's namesake rule allows candidates to simultaneously run for the senate and the vice presidency. He won a Senate seat election with the help of a rented helicopter nicknamed the "City Windmill." He quoted the lyrics to "America the Beautiful" in his "Let Us Continue" speech. His use of the so-called "Treatment" to strong arm dissident party members was discussed in the biography Master of the Senate by Robert Caro. As president, he worked with the 89th congress to pass the Freedom of Information and Higher Education Acts, and gave the "We Shall Overcome" speech in response to the violence in Selma. This president signed the Voting Rights Act and the Social Security Act as part of his Great Society. Name this successor to John F. Kennedy.

A leader of the fief of Kii who led the country during this period introduced sweet potato and sugarcane cultivation and began the compilation of the Kansei law code. Scholarly endeavors in this era were divided into the schools of Ancient Learning, National Learning, and Dutch Learning. This era included the artistic flourishing of the "original happiness period." Another ruler's attempt to stamp out Christianity during this era led to the Shimabara Rebellion. During the disintegration of its namesake government, this period saw the establishment of the Ezo Republic and the Boshin War. Ended by the proclamation of the Charter Oath and rallying behind Emperor Meiji, identify this final Japanese shogunate which lasted from 1600 to 1858.

An early advocate for this country's autonomy was the Sufi poet Magtymguly Pyragy, through it was subsumed into the Russian empire after a twenty-three day siege at the fortress of Geok Tepe. The Russians called this country the Transcapian Province and were opposed at an unsuccessful 1916 revolt in Tejen. As a republic, this country's first president spent over six billion dollars on the massive manmade "Golden Age Lake." That president also made his autobiographical epic called the Rukhnama required reading. One leader of this country renamed all the days of the week for family members and built the Neutrality Arch, which is topped with a giant rotating gold statue of himself. Name this central Asian nation formerly led by Saparmurat Niyazov, who dubbed himself Turkmenbashi.

The leader of the British branch of this denomination was passed over for a position after authoring We Have Reason to Believe in a scandal known as the Jacob's Affair. This group was strengthened though its opposition to the Pittsburgh Platform, which was one of the reasons for the founding of the JTS. One of the immediate sparks for the founding of this movement was an alleged "catering error" at the "Trefa Banquet," and it is governed internationally by the Masorti Olami. This movement split in 1963 when Mordecai Kaplan founded the Reconstructionist movement. It was an extension of Zecharias Frankel's Positive-Historical Judaism, which proposed keeping traditions and laws but being open to reinterpreting them. Name this rival of the Reform movement.

When this man's throne was taken from him, he and his brother fled to Burgundy under the protection of his brother-in-law Charles the Bold, causing a war with France. He first gained the throne by winning the bloody Battle of Towton at the age of 19. This victor at Barnet had a secret marriage to Elizabeth Woodville that soured his relationship with the Duke of Warwick. His brother, Richard of Gloucester was one of his best generals, and his daughter Elizabeth of York was eventually married to Henry VII. Name this Yorkist opponent of Henry VI in the Wars of the Roses who fathered Edward V and was the brother of Richard III.

An account of the truce struck after this battle was published by Madame Fournaise, who owned the "Weaver's Cottage" that housed the negotiations. Following this battle, Léon Gambetta escaped from a siege in a hot air balloon, and its result caused Louis Trochu to establish the Government of National Defense. At this battle, Ducrot likened his strategic position to being in a chamber pot and had his retreat command overridden by Wimpffen after the wounding of General MacMahon. It was MacMahon's indecisiveness which allowed the French forces to be trapped by von Moltke's Army of the Meuse at this battle, which followed French losses at Gravelotte and Metz. Name this battle which included the unexpected capture of Napoleon III, the decisive battle in the Franco-Prussian War.

In an expedition preceding the one lead by this man, the Moorish slave Black Stephen or Estevanico struck out alone ahead of the party and was allegedly killed because of his demands for women. That party was led by Fray Marcos de Niza, who stopped short when he heard of the fate of Stephen but submitted a glowing report to Viceroy Antonio de Mendoza. This man personally strangled his guide "El Turco" after his search for the city of Quivira led him only to boring tribes in Kansas. After defeating some Zuni soldiers but discovering there was no treasure at Cibola, he abandoned his quest for the Seven Cities of Gold and ended up discovering the Grand Canyon and exploring the Colorado River. Name this "last conquistador" who explored the American West.

The descendents of immigrants from the Indian subcontinent who live in this country tend to vote for the United National Congress, while the descendents of African slaves tend to support the People's National Movement. Key events in the history of this country include an attempted Black Power Revolution in 1970 and an attempted coup by supporters of the Islamic fundamentalist Jamaat-al-Muslimeen in 1990. The Economic Aspects of the Abolition of the Slave Trade and Capitalism and Slavery were two scholarly works written by the first Prime Minister of this country, Eric Williams. Identify this Caribbean nation that is the birthplace of British writer V.S. Naipaul and the home of the St. Lucia-born author Derek Walcott.

Six chapels were torched by mobs in London's West End during the reign of this monarch, who had attended the trial of the impeached clergyman Dr. Henry Sacheverell. Noted Scriblerus Club member Robert Harley was co-Secretary of State with Lord Sunderland under a man Sacheverell sneeringly dubbed "Volpone." In addition to Sidney Godolphin being the head of this monarch's first ministry, this ruler was widely laughed at for being fat and dull, and died from a stroke after enduring thirteen miscarriages out of eighteen pregnancies. Presiding over the inaugural feud between the Tories and Whigs, this ruler's generals include the Duke of Marlborough, John Churchill, the victor at Blenheim. Identify this daughter of James II who ruled as the last Stuart monarch, the sister of Mary II.

One revolt in this city was caused by the working class Cabochiens. Abbo Cernuus provides the only account of the siege of this city in 885, which saw the appearance of Rollo, who later became Robert I of Normandy, command the besieging forces. This Western European city contains a building built to house the Crown of Thorns bought from the Byzantines. In addition to La Sainte-Chapelle, this city saw the Day of the Barricades, forcing Henry III out of this Catholic city. It was extensively renovated under Baron Haussmann. And besieged during the Franco-Prussian War. Name this city, the home of the Louvre and capital of France.

One depiction of this event claimed that its participants were enticed by "molasses and codfish." Lampooned in William Charles's cartoon "Leap or No Leap," it resolved that slaves should no longer be counted in the census, and that no President should come from the same state as his predecessor. Defended in a series of letters by Harrison Gray Otis, many of its participants were members of the Essex Junto. Name this 1814 meeting of Federalists opposed to the War of 1812.

In addition to 2001 bombings of the Ealing Broadway shopping center and a media company's headquarters, the 1998 Omagh Bombing was done by this group, which is led by Kevin McKenna and Michael McKevitt. They recently claimed responsibility for the shooting of two British soldiers outside the Massereene Barracks in Northern Ireland. Name this 1997 splitoff group from the Provisional IRA, not to be confused with the Continuity or Official IRA.

This ruler lost the Battle of Chakling and was betrayed during a war with Dai Viet. He reversed the patronage of Buddhism and promoted the worship of Vishnu in concert with the priest Divakarapandita, but died in 1150, just before his empire was overrun by Cham. Name this king of Khmer, who demonstrated his devotion to Vishnu by building the temple complex Angkor Wat.

One member of this dynasty successfully acquired Delagoa Bay from Austria, and another wrote the Defense of Mondern Music. During the rule of this dynasty, the Treaty of Methuen was signed with England, and Jesuits were expelled by the Marquis de Pombal after the Tavora Affair. The Battle of Montijo put this house on the throne, and they later paid a dowry of Tangier and Bombay to marry a female member to Charles II of England. Name this house which ruled Portugal from 1640 to the 1910s.

The Banded Eye god from this people's mythology is sometimes given as an aspect of their Maize god. This civilization expanded as far from their capital as Chalcatzingo, and while many of their monuments were found at Tres Zapotes, this civilization sometimes created stelae. A more nearby major city was this civilization's site at modern day San Lorenzo. Identify this Mesoamerican civilization with a capital at La Venta, who may be better known for constructing large stone heads.

The losing side in this conflict was victorious at Catubig and Makahambus, although the other side won at Tirad Pass and Makote Bridge.
